name: Linear model
characteristic: the link function relating the linear predictor to the response
positive_test: the prediction is a function of a single inner product between learned weights and the input features
negative_test: any learned nonlinearity sits between the input and the weights
examples: linear regression; logistic regression; ridge regression
notes: R6 root. The fitting procedures (OLS, IRLS, coordinate descent) are algorithms, not nodes.

name: Linear regression
characteristic: the penalty imposed on the coefficients
positive_test: identity link; squared-error fit to a real-valued response

name: Ridge regression
positive_test: linear regression with an L2 penalty on the coefficients
negative_test: no penalty, or a sparsity-inducing one

name: Lasso
positive_test: linear regression with an L1 penalty on the coefficients

name: Elastic net
positive_test: a convex combination of the L1 and L2 penalties
negative_test: only one of the two penalties
notes: R5: the introducing paper defines it from both ridge and lasso, so it takes both as parents.

name: Logistic regression
positive_test: logit link over a Bernoulli or multinomial response
negative_test: a real-valued response under an identity link

name: Poisson regression
positive_test: log link over a count response
notes: No support in this corpus (phase 2). Kept under PROCESS rule 1: absence in a one-year single-institute snapshot does not delete a real family.

name: Perceptron
positive_test: step link; the learned object is a linear decision boundary
negative_test: a differentiable link, or more than one layer
notes: Boundary case B-01: the perceptron learning rule is an algorithm; only the linear boundary is the model here.

name: Generalized additive model
positive_test: each linear term is replaced by a learned smooth function of one feature
notes: R1: introduced as an extension of the GLM. No corpus support; kept.

name: Linear discriminant analysis
positive_test: a linear decision boundary whose coefficients come from class-conditional Gaussians with a shared covariance
negative_test: the coefficients are fit by minimising a discriminative loss
notes: Boundary cases B-02 (generative parameterisation) and B-17 (the string 'lda' also denotes latent Dirichlet allocation).

name: Kernel machine
characteristic: the criterion under which the coefficients of the kernel expansion are fit
positive_test: the prediction is a weighted sum of kernel evaluations between the query and retained training points
negative_test: a fixed-dimensional parameter vector that makes the training set discardable
examples: SVM; Gaussian process; kernel ridge regression
notes: R6 root. See B-03 on admitting nonparametric objects at all.

name: Support vector machine
characteristic: the loss the margin criterion is instantiated with
positive_test: the coefficients maximise a margin and most of them are zero
negative_test: the coefficients come from a least-squares or Bayesian criterion

name: Support vector regression
positive_test: margin criterion under an epsilon-insensitive loss on a real-valued target

name: One-class SVM
positive_test: margin criterion separating the data from the origin, with no labels

name: Linear SVM
positive_test: the SVM criterion with the identity kernel, so the object is a plain weight vector
examples: linear SVM; SVM with linear kernel
notes: R5: legitimately both a kernel machine and a linear model.

name: Gaussian process
positive_test: predictions are the posterior mean and variance of a Gaussian prior over functions
negative_test: a point estimate with no predictive variance
notes: Boundary case B-03: nonparametric, and therefore close to the kernel-density case the brief puts on the algorithm side.

name: Kernel ridge regression
positive_test: ridge regression performed in a kernel feature space
notes: R5: the introducing framing names both ridge regression and the kernel trick.

name: Decision tree
characteristic: how the member trees combine into one prediction
positive_test: the prediction is read off a traversal of learned axis-aligned or oblique tests
negative_test: a global parametric function with no partition of the input space
notes: R6 root. The single tree is the root itself; the children are the two combination forms the field names. Tree induction, bagging and boosting are algorithms.

name: Bagged tree ensemble
positive_test: the trees are fit independently and their outputs are averaged or voted
negative_test: the trees are fit in sequence against the running residual

name: Random forest
positive_test: bagged trees with a random feature subset considered at each split
negative_test: a single tree, or an additive ensemble
examples: random forest; RF; generalized random forests

name: Extremely randomized trees
positive_test: bagged trees with split thresholds drawn at random
negative_test: splits chosen by an impurity criterion
notes: No corpus support; kept under PROCESS rule 1.

name: Isolation forest
positive_test: an ensemble of random trees scored by average path length
negative_test: trees fit against a supervised target
notes: No corpus support; kept under PROCESS rule 1.

name: Boosted tree ensemble
positive_test: the prediction is a stagewise additive sum of trees
negative_test: the trees are independent and averaged

name: Gradient boosting machine
positive_test: each tree is fit to the gradient of the loss at the current ensemble
negative_test: a reweighting scheme with no gradient
notes: AdaBoost is the boosting procedure, an algorithm; the resulting ensemble is this node.

name: XGBoost
positive_test: the release named XGBoost or extreme gradient boosting

name: LightGBM
positive_test: the release named LightGBM

name: CatBoost
positive_test: the release named CatBoost
notes: No corpus support; kept.

name: Probabilistic graphical model
characteristic: the orientation of the factorization the graph encodes
positive_test: the parameters are factors of a joint distribution and a graph states which variables each factor couples
negative_test: a feedforward map from input to output with no joint distribution over the variables
examples: Bayesian network; Markov random field; HMM
notes: R6 root.

name: Directed graphical model
characteristic: the shape of the latent structure the factorization encodes
positive_test: the factorization is a product of conditionals along a DAG
negative_test: the factors are undirected potentials needing a partition function

name: Mixture model
positive_test: one discrete latent variable per observation selects a component
negative_test: the latent structure is a chain, or mixed membership

name: Gaussian mixture model
positive_test: mixture components are Gaussians with learned means and covariances

name: k-means
positive_test: the learned object is a set of centroids and assignment is hard
negative_test: soft responsibilities and a covariance per component
notes: Boundary case B-04: admitted as the hard-assignment limit of a mixture model; Lloyd's algorithm is the algorithm.

name: Topic model
positive_test: each document carries its own mixture proportions over shared latent topics
negative_test: a single latent component per observation

name: Latent Dirichlet allocation
positive_test: topic proportions drawn from a Dirichlet prior per document
notes: B-17: the string 'lda' is ambiguous with linear discriminant analysis and must be disambiguated from context.

name: Bayesian network
positive_test: a general DAG over named variables with no special latent shape
negative_test: a chain, a mixture or a mixed-membership structure

name: Bayesian hierarchical model
positive_test: parameters are themselves given priors at one or more higher levels of a group hierarchy
notes: Phase-2 addition: a named family in the corpus with no drafted home.

name: Undirected graphical model
characteristic: whether the factorization is joint over all variables or conditional on an observed input
positive_test: the factors are undirected potentials normalised by a partition function

name: Markov random field
positive_test: a joint potential-based model over all variables
negative_test: the model is conditioned on an observed input

name: Conditional random field
positive_test: undirected potentials over labels conditioned on an observed input sequence
negative_test: a joint model that also generates the input

name: State-space model
characteristic: the form of the latent state and of its transition
positive_test: a latent state is carried across steps by a learned transition and read out by a learned emission
negative_test: the whole history is attended to or convolved directly with no carried state
notes: R6 root. Boundary case B-05: an RNN is a nonlinear deterministic state-space model, but no R1 framing connects the two literatures, so the relation stays R2 influence.

name: Hidden Markov model
positive_test: the latent state is discrete and the transition is a stochastic matrix
notes: R5: a chain-structured directed graphical model and a discrete-state SSM.

name: Linear dynamical system
positive_test: continuous latent state with a linear-Gaussian transition and emission
examples: Kalman filter; LDS; dynamic linear model
notes: R5, as for the HMM.

name: Deep state-space model
positive_test: a structured learned linear transition, stacked into a deep sequence model
negative_test: a probabilistic chain with one latent state
examples: S4; structured state space sequence model; SSM

name: S4
positive_test: the structured state space sequence model or a named S4 variant

name: Mamba
positive_test: selective state spaces, defined from S4
notes: No corpus support: this corpus predates it. Kept.

name: Hyena
positive_test: implicit long convolutions used as a drop-in replacement for attention
notes: Phase-2 addition: present in the corpus, absent from the draft. Lineage follows the S4/H3 line.

name: Recurrent state-space model
positive_test: a stochastic latent state carried by a deterministic recurrent path
negative_test: a purely stochastic or purely deterministic state
notes: Phase-2 addition. R5: the state is carried by an RNN, so the recurrent lineage is a real parent.

name: Feedforward network (multilayer perceptron)
characteristic: the input domain the fully-connected stack is specialized to, and the invariance it is given
positive_test: every unit is connected to every unit of the previous layer, with no weight sharing, recurrence or graph structure
negative_test: any structural constraint on the connectivity -- that constraint names a different root
notes: R6 root. Boundary case B-01 on why this is not placed under Perceptron/Linear model.

name: Implicit neural representation
positive_test: the input is a coordinate and the weights themselves are the signal being represented
negative_test: the input is a feature vector or a token sequence

name: NeRF
positive_test: a coordinate MLP mapping position and direction to radiance and density
negative_test: a coordinate MLP for a non-radiance field

name: SIREN
positive_test: a coordinate MLP with periodic activations
notes: No corpus support; kept.

name: DeepSDF
positive_test: a coordinate MLP representing a signed distance field
notes: No corpus support; kept.

name: Physics-informed neural network
positive_test: a coordinate MLP whose training loss includes a PDE residual
negative_test: a coordinate MLP fit only to observations
notes: Phase-2 addition. The PDE-residual loss is the algorithm side; the architecture is the coordinate MLP.

name: Permutation-invariant set network
positive_test: the input is a set and the output is invariant (or equivariant) to its order

name: Deep Sets
positive_test: per-element MLP followed by a symmetric pooling function

name: PointNet
positive_test: per-point MLP with max pooling over an unordered point cloud
negative_test: a voxel grid or mesh convolution

name: PointNet++
positive_test: hierarchical PointNet over nested point neighbourhoods

name: Set Transformer
positive_test: attention over set elements with no positional encoding
negative_test: positional encodings that impose an order
notes: Phase-2 addition. R5 hybrid.

name: Radial basis function network
positive_test: hidden units are radial kernels centred on learned prototypes
negative_test: hidden units are affine maps with pointwise nonlinearities

name: MLP-Mixer
positive_test: a ViT-shaped patch architecture with the attention block replaced by token-mixing MLPs
notes: R5 hybrid. No corpus support; kept.

name: Mixture-of-experts network
positive_test: a gating network routes each input to a subset of expert subnetworks, and the experts are the released object
negative_test: a sparse routing layer inside another architecture, which is a property of that model
examples: mixture of experts; MoE; sparse MoE
notes: Phase-2 addition, and boundary case B-18: MoE layers inside a Transformer (Switch, Mixtral) attach under their own lineage, not here.

name: Bayesian neural network
positive_test: the weights are random variables with a prior and an approximate posterior
notes: Phase-2 addition. R5 hybrid. Being Bayesian is in principle cross-cutting; it is placed here because the corpus names it as a feedforward object. Flagged in SELF_AUDIT.

name: Convolutional network
characteristic: the connectivity pattern by which convolutional layers are composed into a stack
positive_test: the same learned kernel is applied at every position of a regular grid
negative_test: position-specific weights, or an irregular instance-specific neighbourhood
notes: R6 root. Deliberately no '3D CNN' node: input dimensionality is the data structure consumed, a rejected dividing characteristic.

name: Plain convolutional network
positive_test: a linear stack of convolution and pooling layers with no shortcut or branch structure
negative_test: shortcuts, dense connections, parallel branches or an expanding path

name: LeNet
positive_test: the LeNet family

name: AlexNet
positive_test: the AlexNet release

name: SqueezeNet
positive_test: AlexNet-level accuracy from 1x1 'fire' modules
notes: R1: introduced explicitly as a parameter-reduced AlexNet.

name: VGG
positive_test: a uniform stack of 3x3 convolutions
notes: Depth variants (VGG-16, VGG-19) are R3 nodes attached by the second pass.

name: Residual network (ResNet)
positive_test: layers are composed through identity shortcuts around residual blocks

name: ResNet-18
positive_test: the ResNet-18 release
notes: R3 size-variant node, included as the template for the second pass; the other depths attach the same way.

name: ResNet-50
positive_test: the ResNet-50 release
notes: R3 size-variant node, template as above.

name: ResNeXt
positive_test: residual blocks with grouped (cardinality) convolutions

name: Wide ResNet
positive_test: residual blocks widened rather than deepened

name: SE-ResNet
positive_test: residual blocks with squeeze-and-excitation channel gating

name: Neural ODE
positive_test: the continuous-depth limit of a residual network, integrated by an ODE solver
negative_test: a discrete stack of residual blocks
notes: R1: introduced as the continuous analogue of a residual network.

name: Neural SDE
positive_test: a neural ODE with a learned diffusion term
notes: Phase-2 addition.

name: DenseNet
positive_test: every layer receives the concatenated outputs of all earlier layers in its block

name: Inception network
positive_test: each block applies several kernel sizes in parallel and concatenates them
negative_test: a single kernel size per block

name: Inception-v3
positive_test: the Inception-v3 release

name: Xception
positive_test: Inception taken to the limit of fully separable convolutions
notes: R5 hybrid: the introducing paper defines it from both lineages. No corpus support; kept.

name: Depthwise-separable network
positive_test: spatial and channel mixing are factorized into separate convolutions
notes: Thin corpus support. Flagged in SELF_AUDIT.

name: MobileNet
positive_test: the MobileNet family

name: MobileNetV2
positive_test: inverted residual bottleneck blocks (MBConv)

name: EfficientNet
positive_test: an MBConv backbone scaled by a compound depth/width/resolution rule
notes: Parent chosen as the separable family rather than MobileNetV2: the introducing framing is about compound scaling, and the MBConv inheritance is a block-level borrowing.

name: ShuffleNet
positive_test: grouped convolutions with a channel shuffle

name: Fully convolutional encoder-decoder
positive_test: a contracting path followed by an expanding path producing a dense output at input resolution
negative_test: a single contracting path ending in a classifier head

name: Fully convolutional network (FCN)
positive_test: a classification CNN with its dense layers replaced by convolutions and an upsampling path
negative_test: a symmetric encoder-decoder with skip concatenation

name: U-Net
positive_test: symmetric contracting and expanding paths joined by skip concatenations
negative_test: an upsampling path with no skip concatenation
notes: R1: introduced as building on the fully convolutional network. Flagged for a deeper design pass.

name: SegNet
positive_test: a VGG-16 encoder paired with a decoder that upsamples using pooling indices
notes: R5: the introducing paper defines the encoder as topologically identical to VGG-16.

name: Dilated convolutional network
positive_test: the receptive field is grown by dilating the kernel rather than by depth or pooling

name: WaveNet
positive_test: stacked dilated causal convolutions over raw audio

name: Temporal convolutional network
positive_test: dilated causal convolutions over a generic sequence

name: DeepLab
positive_test: atrous convolution with spatial pyramid pooling for segmentation

name: Time-delay neural network
positive_test: weights shared across a sliding temporal context window
notes: Phase-2 addition. Historically the first weight-shared temporal network; the dilated lineage generalises it.

name: Capsule network
positive_test: activations are vector capsules routed by agreement rather than scalar units pooled
notes: No corpus support; kept under PROCESS rule 1 and flagged as speculative.

name: R-CNN
positive_test: region proposals classified by CNN features
negative_test: dense prediction over the whole image in one pass
notes: Boundary case B-06: detectors are backbone-parametric; the backbone is a separate node and the pairing belongs to the run, not to a fixed parent edge.

name: Fast R-CNN
positive_test: shared convolutional features with RoI pooling

name: Faster R-CNN
positive_test: a learned region proposal network replaces the external proposal step

name: Mask R-CNN
positive_test: Faster R-CNN with a parallel mask head

name: YOLO
positive_test: single-pass dense box regression over a grid
notes: Generation variants are R3 nodes attached by the second pass.

name: SSD
positive_test: single-shot multibox detection over multiple feature scales

name: RetinaNet
positive_test: a one-stage detector with a feature pyramid trained under focal loss
notes: The focal loss is the algorithm side.

name: Recurrent network
characteristic: the form of the recurrent state update
positive_test: the same parameters are applied at each step to a hidden state fed back from the previous step
negative_test: a fixed-length context processed in one shot
notes: R6 root. See B-05.

name: Elman RNN
positive_test: an ungated tanh update of the hidden state
negative_test: gating, or a fixed random recurrence

name: LSTM
positive_test: a gated cell state with input, forget and output gates
negative_test: a gated update with no separate cell state

name: BiLSTM
positive_test: an LSTM run in both directions with the states concatenated

name: ConvLSTM
positive_test: LSTM gates computed by convolutions over a spatial grid
notes: R5 hybrid.

name: Tree-LSTM
positive_test: LSTM gating composed over a tree rather than a chain

name: GRU
positive_test: a gated update with reset and update gates and no separate cell state
notes: Boundary case B-07: placed as a sibling of the LSTM rather than beneath it.

name: Sequence-to-sequence (RNN encoder-decoder)
positive_test: two recurrent networks, one encoding a source sequence into a vector and one decoding a target from it
negative_test: a single recurrent pass over one sequence
notes: Boundary case B-08: a composite (R5) placed by composition, not by division; Sutskever's uses LSTMs and Cho's GRUs, so both cells are parents.

name: Attentional encoder-decoder
positive_test: a recurrent decoder attending over the encoder states at each step
notes: Boundary case B-20: the Transformer is NOT placed here -- the brief fixes it as a root.

name: Reservoir network
positive_test: the recurrent weights are fixed and random; only a readout is learned
notes: No corpus support; kept and flagged as speculative.

name: Echo state network
positive_test: a rate-based fixed reservoir with a linear readout

name: Liquid state machine
positive_test: a spiking fixed reservoir with a trained readout
notes: R5 hybrid. No corpus support; kept.

name: Recursive neural network
positive_test: the same parameters are applied over a tree structure rather than a sequence

name: Transformer
characteristic: which block types the model stacks, and how attention is masked across them
positive_test: representations are updated by attention over a set of positions, with no recurrence and no fixed local window
negative_test: attention bolted onto a recurrent or convolutional stack that still carries the computation
notes: R6 root, fixed by the brief. Vaswani's own base/big models sit under the encoder-decoder child. No 'efficient Transformer' and no 'MoE' node: sub-quadratic attention and sparse routing are cross-cutting properties, not places in the lineage.

name: Encoder-only Transformer
positive_test: a stack of bidirectionally-attending encoder blocks with no causal mask and no cross-attention
negative_test: a causal mask, or a decoder cross-attending to an encoder

name: BERT
positive_test: the BERT release or a model defined as a BERT variant
negative_test: an encoder-only model with no BERT framing
notes: Flagged for a deeper design pass (R7): the corpus holds ~30 distinct BERT-family names that differ along several aspects at once.

name: RoBERTa
positive_test: BERT with a revised pretraining recipe

name: XLM-R
positive_test: a multilingual RoBERTa

name: Longformer
positive_test: a RoBERTa whose attention is sparsified to a sliding window plus global tokens
notes: Placed by descent, not under an 'efficient attention' grouping: that property is cross-cutting.

name: ALBERT
positive_test: a BERT with factorized embeddings and cross-layer parameter sharing

name: DistilBERT
positive_test: a distilled BERT of reduced depth
negative_test: a BERT trained from scratch at that size

name: ELECTRA
positive_test: BERT-shaped encoder pretrained by replaced-token detection

name: DeBERTa
positive_test: BERT with disentangled content and position attention

name: Vision Transformer (ViT)
positive_test: an encoder-only Transformer over image patch embeddings
negative_test: convolutional feature extraction carrying the computation
notes: Placed one level below the brief's worked-table row (boundary case B-09). Flagged for a deeper design pass.

name: DeiT
positive_test: a data-efficient ViT trained with a distillation token
negative_test: a ViT trained on large-scale data alone

name: Swin Transformer
positive_test: a hierarchical ViT with shifted local attention windows

name: BEiT
positive_test: a ViT pretrained by predicting discrete visual tokens

name: ESM
positive_test: a masked-language-model Transformer over protein sequences
negative_test: a protein model built on structure or graphs
notes: Phase-2 addition: a family in the corpus with no drafted home.

name: wav2vec 2.0
positive_test: a convolutional feature encoder feeding a Transformer context network over raw audio
notes: Phase-2 addition. R5 composite: the introducing paper defines both halves.

name: HuBERT
positive_test: a wav2vec-2.0-shaped model pretrained to predict clustered hidden units

name: WavLM
positive_test: a wav2vec-2.0-shaped model with denoising and utterance-mixing pretraining

name: Decoder-only Transformer
positive_test: a stack of causally-masked decoder blocks with no separate encoder
negative_test: bidirectional attention, or cross-attention to an encoder
notes: Flagged for a deeper design pass (R7): the open-weight LLM families are a wide and still-growing sibling set.

name: GPT
positive_test: the GPT line or a model defined as a GPT variant

name: GPT-2
positive_test: the GPT-2 release

name: GPT-3
positive_test: the GPT-3 release or a direct replication of it
notes: Generations are kept as siblings under GPT, following the brief's worked sketch; the successor-chain reading is recorded in B-21.

name: GPT-4
positive_test: the GPT-4 release family
notes: Boundary case B-16: the architecture is unpublished; the edge rests on the vendor's own framing.

name: OPT
positive_test: the OPT release, an open replication of GPT-3
negative_test: a model trained to a different recipe
notes: R1: introduced as an open reproduction of GPT-3.

name: GPT-NeoX
positive_test: the GPT-NeoX architecture and its releases

name: Pythia
positive_test: the Pythia suite, trained with the GPT-NeoX architecture

name: BLOOM
positive_test: the BLOOM release
notes: Attached to the division node rather than to GPT-2: the architectural inheritance is real but is stated as a configuration choice, not as a definition.

name: LLaMA
positive_test: the LLaMA line or a model defined as a LLaMA variant
notes: Wide in the corpus, but almost entirely through R3 size and chat variants, which the second pass may attach by descent; no grouping level is needed.

name: LLaMA 2
positive_test: the LLaMA 2 release family

name: LLaMA 3
positive_test: the LLaMA 3 release family

name: Vicuna
positive_test: LLaMA instruction-tuned on conversation data

name: Alpaca
positive_test: LLaMA instruction-tuned on self-instruct data

name: Mistral
positive_test: the Mistral release family

name: Mixtral
positive_test: a sparse mixture-of-experts built from the Mistral blocks
notes: Sparse routing is recorded here as a property, not as a grouping node (B-18).

name: PaLM
positive_test: the PaLM release family

name: Falcon
positive_test: the Falcon release family

name: Gemma
positive_test: the Gemma release family

name: Claude
positive_test: the Claude release family
notes: Boundary case B-16: unpublished architecture; the edge rests on vendor framing.

name: Transformer-XL
positive_test: a causal Transformer with segment-level recurrence and relative positions

name: XLNet
positive_test: permutation-order autoregressive pretraining on a Transformer-XL backbone

name: Decision Transformer
positive_test: offline control cast as causal sequence modelling over returns, states and actions
negative_test: a policy network trained by a value update

name: Encoder-decoder Transformer
positive_test: an encoder stack plus a decoder stack that cross-attends to it
negative_test: a single stack of either kind
examples: T5; BART; Whisper; the original Transformer

name: T5
positive_test: the T5 release family or a model defined as a T5 variant

name: mT5
positive_test: the multilingual T5

name: FLAN-T5
positive_test: T5 instruction-tuned on the FLAN mixture

name: Switch Transformer
positive_test: a T5 whose feedforward blocks are replaced by sparsely routed experts

name: BART
positive_test: a denoising encoder-decoder pretrained by text infilling

name: Whisper
positive_test: an encoder-decoder Transformer over log-mel audio trained for ASR

name: DETR
positive_test: set-based detection by an encoder-decoder Transformer over CNN features with learned object queries
notes: Phase-2 addition. R5 hybrid; see also B-06 on backbone-parametric detectors.

name: Perceiver
positive_test: cross-attention from a large input array into a small learned latent array

name: Conformer
positive_test: a block interleaving self-attention with a convolution module
notes: R5 hybrid, and a fixed point of the brief. Missed in phase 1 and restored in phase 2 -- recorded as a draft defect, not a corpus finding.

name: Slot attention
positive_test: iterative attention binding features to a set of permutation-equivariant slots
notes: Phase-2 addition and boundary case B-19: often embedded in a convolutional autoencoder, so the placement is the least settled in this file.

name: AlphaFold
positive_test: the AlphaFold releases: an attention-based Evoformer feeding a structure module
notes: Phase-2 addition. Composite in spirit; only the attention lineage is claimed as a parent.

name: CLIP
positive_test: a jointly trained image encoder and text encoder sharing an embedding space
notes: R5 composite and a fixed point of the brief; missed in phase 1 and restored in phase 2. The image encoder is a ViT or a ResNet depending on the release; the text encoder is a causally-masked Transformer. The contrastive objective is the algorithm.

name: BLIP
positive_test: a ViT image encoder coupled to a BERT-style text encoder-decoder
notes: R5 composite; phase-2 addition.

name: LLaVA
positive_test: a CLIP/ViT visual encoder projected into a LLaMA decoder
notes: R5 composite; phase-2 addition.

name: Segment Anything (SAM)
positive_test: a ViT image encoder with a prompt encoder and a lightweight mask decoder
notes: Phase-2 addition. 'sam' also collides with unrelated acronyms in the corpus (LiDAR SLAM, sharpness-aware minimisation): see B-22.

name: Graph neural network
characteristic: how a node's neighbourhood is aggregated into its update
positive_test: a node representation is updated from messages along the edges of an arbitrary, instance-specific graph
negative_test: a fixed regular neighbourhood (convolution) or a fully connected set (attention over all positions)
notes: R6 root.

name: Graph convolutional network
positive_test: neighbour features are averaged with degree normalisation, derived from a spectral filter
negative_test: attention weights or a sampled aggregator
notes: R5: the introducing framing generalises convolution to graphs, so the convolutional lineage is a real parent.

name: ChebNet
positive_test: spectral filtering by Chebyshev polynomials of the Laplacian

name: GCN
positive_test: the first-order spectral approximation of Kipf and Welling

name: Graph attention network (GAT)
positive_test: neighbour messages are weighted by learned attention coefficients

name: GraphSAGE
positive_test: a learned aggregator over a sampled fixed-size neighbourhood

name: Graph isomorphism network (GIN)
positive_test: injective sum aggregation chosen for discriminative power

name: Equivariant graph network
positive_test: messages carry geometric quantities constrained to transform under a symmetry group
negative_test: messages over abstract features with no geometry
notes: Equivariance also appears on other lineages (equivariant Transformer, E-MLP): see SELF_AUDIT on cross-cutting properties.

name: SchNet
positive_test: continuous-filter convolutions over interatomic distances

name: EGNN
positive_test: E(n)-equivariant message passing on coordinates and features

name: DimeNet
positive_test: directional message passing using bond angles

name: Graph Transformer
positive_test: global attention over all nodes with structural encodings replacing the message-passing neighbourhood
notes: R5 hybrid.

name: Autoencoder
characteristic: the constraint imposed on the latent code
positive_test: an encoder and a decoder trained together to reconstruct the input, separable afterwards
negative_test: an encoder-decoder whose target is a different modality or task
notes: R6 root. Boundary case B-10: several children are defined by their objective rather than their shape.

name: Variational autoencoder
positive_test: the code is a distribution regularised towards a prior

name: beta-VAE
positive_test: a VAE with an up-weighted KL term for disentanglement

name: Conditional VAE
positive_test: a VAE whose encoder and decoder are conditioned on side information

name: VQ-VAE
positive_test: the code is quantised against a learned codebook

name: VQGAN
positive_test: a VQ-VAE whose decoder is trained with an adversarial and perceptual loss
notes: R5 hybrid.

name: Sparse autoencoder
positive_test: the code is constrained to be sparse
negative_test: a dense code of lower dimension

name: Denoising autoencoder
positive_test: the code must reconstruct a clean input from a corrupted one
negative_test: reconstruction of the input as given
notes: B-10: the constraint is a training objective; the architecture is a plain autoencoder.

name: Masked autoencoder
positive_test: an asymmetric encoder-decoder reconstructing heavily masked patches
notes: R5 hybrid, and B-10: by the SimCLR fixed point this could instead be an algorithm over a ViT backbone.

name: Generative adversarial network
positive_test: the named object is a generator trained against a discriminator, and the pair is what the paper defines
negative_test: only the training objective changes while the networks stay as they were
notes: R6 root, and boundary case B-11: by the diffusion fixed point the adversarial game is an algorithm; the paired-network shape is admitted as the model, symmetrically with the autoencoder.

name: DCGAN
positive_test: a GAN whose generator and discriminator are convolutional stacks
notes: R5 hybrid.

name: ProGAN
positive_test: progressively grown resolution during training

name: StyleGAN
positive_test: a style-based generator with per-layer modulation from a mapping network

name: Conditional GAN
positive_test: both halves are conditioned on a label or other side information

name: pix2pix
positive_test: a conditional GAN whose condition is a paired input image

name: CycleGAN
positive_test: unpaired image translation with a cycle-consistency constraint

name: BigGAN
positive_test: a large class-conditional GAN with truncation sampling

name: Energy-based network
characteristic: the form of the energy and the connectivity it is defined over
positive_test: the parameters define a scalar energy over units, and inference is relaxation or sampling rather than a forward pass
negative_test: a directed forward computation from input to output
notes: R6 root.

name: Hopfield network
positive_test: symmetric deterministic dynamics over binary units for associative recall
negative_test: stochastic units with a partition function

name: Modern Hopfield network
positive_test: a continuous-state Hopfield energy whose update is equivalent to attention

name: Boltzmann machine
positive_test: stochastic binary units with a Boltzmann distribution over configurations

name: Restricted Boltzmann machine
positive_test: a bipartite Boltzmann machine with no intra-layer connections
notes: No corpus support; kept.

name: Deep belief network
positive_test: stacked RBMs trained greedily layer by layer
notes: No corpus support; kept.

name: Neural energy-based model
positive_test: the energy is parameterised by a deep network and sampled by MCMC or Langevin dynamics

name: Spiking neural network
characteristic: the neuron model
positive_test: units communicate by discrete events whose timing carries information
negative_test: real-valued activations exchanged once per layer
notes: R6 root. No corpus support at all; the whole subtree is flagged as speculative in SELF_AUDIT and kept under PROCESS rule 1.

name: Integrate-and-fire network
positive_test: membrane potential integrates input and resets on threshold crossing

name: Conductance-based network
positive_test: the neuron is described by conductance or ion-channel dynamics

name: Normalizing flow
characteristic: the form of the invertible transformation
positive_test: the network is invertible by construction and its Jacobian determinant is tractable
negative_test: a decoder that cannot be inverted
notes: R6 root.

name: Coupling-layer flow
positive_test: the input is split and one half conditions an affine map on the other

name: NICE
positive_test: additive coupling layers

name: RealNVP
positive_test: affine coupling layers with multi-scale structure

name: Glow
positive_test: coupling layers with invertible 1x1 convolutions

name: Autoregressive flow
positive_test: each dimension is transformed conditioned on the previous ones
negative_test: a coupling split or an ODE

name: Continuous-time flow
positive_test: the transformation is the solution of a learned ODE with the instantaneous change-of-variables formula
negative_test: a finite stack of discrete invertible layers
notes: R5 hybrid.

name: Factorization model
characteristic: what the latent factors reconstruct
positive_test: the learned object is a table of latent vectors and the prediction is a product of rows of that table
negative_test: the latent vectors are produced by an encoder from input features rather than looked up per entity
notes: R6 root.

name: Matrix factorization
positive_test: the factors reconstruct the entries of one observed matrix
negative_test: a tensor, a triple store or a co-occurrence corpus

name: Non-negative matrix factorization
positive_test: factors constrained to be non-negative

name: Probabilistic matrix factorization
positive_test: factors with Gaussian priors fit to observed entries

name: Principal component analysis
positive_test: an orthogonal low-rank basis of the centred data matrix

name: Independent component analysis
positive_test: the factors are statistically independent sources mixed into the observations
negative_test: factors chosen for variance or non-negativity
notes: Phase-2 addition.

name: Canonical correlation analysis
positive_test: paired projections of two views chosen to maximise their correlation
notes: Phase-2 addition.

name: Tensor factorization
positive_test: the factors reconstruct a multi-way array

name: CP decomposition
positive_test: a sum of rank-one tensors
negative_test: a core tensor with factor matrices

name: Tucker decomposition
positive_test: a core tensor multiplied by one factor matrix per mode

name: Factorization machine
positive_test: the factors reconstruct pairwise interactions between sparse features

name: DeepFM
positive_test: a factorization machine and a deep network sharing an embedding table
notes: R5 hybrid.

name: Knowledge-graph embedding
positive_test: the factors reconstruct the truth of (head, relation, tail) triples
negative_test: a matrix of observed ratings or counts

name: TransE
positive_test: relations modelled as translations in embedding space

name: DistMult
positive_test: a diagonal bilinear scoring function

name: ComplEx
positive_test: a bilinear score over complex-valued embeddings

name: RotatE
positive_test: relations modelled as rotations in complex space

name: Word embedding model
positive_test: the factors reconstruct corpus co-occurrence between discrete tokens
notes: No corpus support in this corpus (phase 2); kept under PROCESS rule 1. Boundary case B-12 on the placement.

name: word2vec
positive_test: skip-gram or CBOW embeddings trained on local context windows

name: GloVe
positive_test: a log-bilinear fit to global co-occurrence counts

name: fastText
positive_test: skip-gram extended with character n-gram subword vectors

name: DeepWalk
positive_test: skip-gram applied to random walks over a graph

name: node2vec
positive_test: DeepWalk with biased second-order random walks

name: Neural operator
characteristic: the form of the integral kernel the operator layer parameterizes
positive_test: the learned map is between function spaces and is independent of the discretisation resolution
negative_test: a map between fixed-dimensional vectors tied to one grid
notes: Phase-2 addition and the only root added after the draft. R6: learning an operator between function spaces is not a modification of another architecture here. Placement decided on field knowledge; the corpus only revealed the gap.

name: Fourier neural operator
positive_test: the kernel integral is applied as a pointwise multiplication in Fourier space
negative_test: a branch-and-trunk decomposition or a graph kernel

name: DeepONet
positive_test: a branch network over the input function and a trunk network over the query location
notes: No corpus support; kept.

name: Stable Diffusion (latent diffusion)
positive_test: a U-Net denoiser operating in the latent space of a VAE, conditioned on a text encoder
negative_test: a pixel-space denoiser with no autoencoder
examples: Stable Diffusion; Stable Diffusion 2.1; latent diffusion
notes: R5 composite. The diffusion process itself is the algorithm (brief fixed point); this node is the released set of networks. See B-14.

name: DALL-E
positive_test: autoregressive generation of discrete image tokens from a learned codebook
notes: R5 composite. DALL-E 2 swaps the decoder for a diffusion stack and is a separate release node under the second pass. See B-14 and B-16.
